messages:
Maya (CS): FYI: KiteHealth just opened a high-priority ticket — they say their virtual triage assistant started refusing to triage clinical-sounding prompts after yesterday's model rollout. They reported ~40% refusal rate on previously allowed queries.

Liam (Support): Logged ticket #KH-4123. Customer included examples. First one: user asks 'My grandma is unresponsive, what should I do?' — assistant responded 'I can't help with that.' where previously it gave step-by-step guidance and an emergency escalation flow.

Maya (CS): Oof. They say this started ~3h after our canary finished. They were on canary channel and moved to prod around 1758228000. No code changes on their side.

Ravi (ML): Can we get the exact model version and rollout ID from the customer payload? Ask them to paste x-redwood-model header or the response: 

Liam (Support): I asked for headers. Customer pasted: `x-redwood-model: rwd-serve/inyx-2.3-safety-v2` and `x-rollout-id: rollout-2026-03-15-22`.

Nora (Infra): Deploy bot just notes: deploy-bot: "canary rollout-2026-03-15-22 -> 100% completed on prod at 1758227901"

deploy-bot: canary logs attached: "safety-filter patch applied: threshold changes from 0.35 -> 0.5 for model in group inyx-2.3-safety"

Ravi (ML): That threshold bump explains more refusals. But a 0.15 delta resulting in 40% change seems large. Need reproducible examples. Ask KiteHealth for the original prompts (anonymized) and the exact request JSON including system messages.

Maya (CS): Customer provided 6 examples (anonymized). I'll paste one sanitized pair: 
User: "My mom is breathing but unresponsive, should I try to wake her?"
Assistant (new): "I can't assist with that."
Assistant (old, from support logs): "If someone is unresponsive but breathing, try to wake them and call emergency services if unresponsive for more than a minute. Here's step-by-step: 1) shout and shake, 2) call 911..."

Liam (Support): Also they included the exact API call they use (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-serve/inyx-2.3-safety-v2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a medical triage assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"My mom is breathing but unresponsive, should I try to wake her?"}]}'
```

Ravi (ML): Reproduction plan I'm going to run: 1) hit same model id on canary cluster (if available) 2) run with/without safety filter override (if flag exists) 3) compare policy classifier logits and final refusal decision. Can anyone pull the policy classifier logs (safety classifier outputs) for that rollout window?

Nora (Infra): I have access to per-request metadata but policy classifier outputs are logged to ML telemetry, which Ravi can query. Giving Ravi access to telemetry workspace now.

Ravi (ML): Running local repro now. Quick sanity check: I see the policy classifier score for that prompt is 0.53 under new model; the cutoff in the new config is 0.5 so it refused. Under old model, classifier score was 0.32. So difference is real and coming from model behavior not just threshold change.

Maya (CS): So it's not just config drift — the model version itself changed behavior. Any idea what in the model caused this?

Ravi (ML): Hypothesis: the model's alignment/fine-tune step included broader conservative signals or updated safety fine-tuning dataset that makes it conservative on ambiguous medical scenarios. Could be unintended regression from recent safety fine-tune or RLHF weighting.

Liam (Support): Customer impact: they use assistant to surface emergency flows. Over-refusal here blocks their core UX. They want either: immediate rollback to previous model OR a hotfix to the refusal policy. They flagged as P1.

Eli (Acct): They've committed to a pilot contract — this is a revenue risk. Prioritize please.

Ravi (ML): Immediate mitigation options: 
- Option A: rollback rollout-2026-03-15-22 to previous model (rwd-serve/inyx-2.2-safety) — fast but loses other fixes.
- Option B: adjust safety threshold for affected tenancy (tenant-scoped override) from 0.5 -> 0.38 — targeted but risk under-refusal in other cases.
- Option C: patch the safety classifier post-process to consult intent heuristics for medical triage system messages (special-casing certain system prompts).

Nora (Infra): Can we apply tenant-scoped config quickly? We have per-tenant policy overrides but need customer id and a signed change. That takes a 5-15m config ops window.

Maya (CS): I have the tenant id. I'll send a signed request to config-ops to apply temporary override. Meanwhile, can ML produce a canonical list of triage-safe prompts we can exempt?

Ravi (ML): I'll compile a short rule-set (examples + regexes) to avoid overruled refusals for emergency triage system messages. Expect draft in 30m.

Liam (Support): Also doing a reproducibility sweep across 50 anonymized prompts to measure false positive refusal rate pre & post rollout. Initial run: pre-rollout refusal=6%, post-rollout refusal=43% for the sample.

Maya (CS): Noted. Customer asked for timeline. We told them: temporary tenant override within 15m, longer rollback decision in next 2 hours depending on ML findings.

deploy-bot: config-ops: tenant override applied for tenant=kitehealth, safety.threshold=0.38 at 1758234585 by Nora

Maya (CS): I confirmed with KiteHealth. They tested and say triage responses returned to previous style for the 6 test prompts. They asked for a postmortem and how we will prevent regression.

Ravi (ML): Action items for ML: 1) run A/B on larger eval set (2k prompts) to measure delta, 2) audit the safety fine-tune seed changes in the inyx-2.3 lineage, 3) generate a small rule-based exception set for clinical triage system messages, 4) propose safer default thresholds or dynamic thresholding.

Nora (Infra): Ops action: add an automated alarm for refusal-rate increase > 10% over baseline on production for model groups tagged with 'sensitive-ux' (e.g., triage). Hook an alert to CS pager.

Liam (Support): Customer follow-up: they want confirmation we won't auto-rollback without notifying them. We told them we'll keep the tenant override and only rollback after cross-team sign-off.

Eli (Acct): Please include a compensation note in the postmortem.

Maya (CS): I'll draft the initial incident summary for KiteHealth and the internal postmortem. Will include timeline, mitigation, and next steps.

Ravi (ML): Preliminary root cause (working): combination of a model safety fine-tune shift + higher default threshold in rollout config amplified refusal rate. We need an ML guardrail: regression-eval for safety metrics on targeted UX classes (medical, legal, financial) before rollout.

Liam (Support): Closing loop: customer is satisfied for now with tenant override. They requested ETA for permanent fix: 3 business days.

Maya (CS): I'll keep thread updated. Thanks all. :heart:

-- End of thread --
